headline: Quiet stabilizing session: KSE-100 bounced +153pts (+0.09%) to 174,929.69 after Tuesday's Hormuz-driven selloff, helped by Pakistan raising a record $3B dual-tranche Eurobond (nearly $6B in orders — a strong external-accounts signal). Portfolio value ~Rs 10.20M, P/L +Rs 153K (+1.53% on cost), up slightly from +1.38% (Rs 139K) yesterday. No holding moved >5% since the last review and nothing crossed a notification threshold (index move well under 2.5%, drawdown still under 10%). GLAXO kept sliding (Rs 323.08, now −8.8% on cost) on the same DRAP pricing-review overhang; EFERT ticked up further (Rs 191.40) on continued urea price-umbrella discipline confirmed in its Q2 briefing (no discounting plan, expects H2 seasonal demand to clear the inventory glut). AVN's Aug 25 EXIT call remains unexecuted (24,500 shares still held) — no new company news, thesis unchanged.
market: KSE-100 closed Thu Sep 3 at 174,929.69, up 153.09 pts (+0.09%) from Wed's 174,776.60 — a volatile session (intraday high 175,796, low 174,894) that ultimately held the line after Tuesday's −0.96% Hormuz-driven drop. Positive catalyst: the finance ministry said Pakistan raised a record $3B through a dual-tranche Eurobond that drew nearly $6B in orders (almost 2x oversubscribed) — a strong vote of confidence in external accounts. Buying was seen across autos, cement, banks, fertilizer, E&P, OMCs and power. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) is ~7.7%, essentially flat vs yesterday's ~7.8% — still short of the 10% line that would justify deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve into MZNPETF/MIIETF, but the gap isn't closing today given the bounce. Hormuz/Iran-US situation: still ongoing (an oil-supply-disruption risk for an importer like Pakistan) but no fresh escalation reported today; Brent remains elevated. SBP holds at 11.5% since the Jul 27 pause, no September MPC meeting news yet. DRAP drug-pricing review (Aug 28-29) remains just a policy review under study — no enactment — but GLAXO extended its slide today (Rs 323.08, −8.8% on cost) while SEARL firmed slightly (Rs 84.83, +2.3% on cost); still reads as sector overhang, not a GLAXO-specific break. EFERT — Q2 corporate briefing confirmed management's stance: no plans to narrow the Rs 150/bag premium despite the lowest H1 urea sales in a decade (537K tons, 1H2026 revenue −12% YoY, net profit −16% to Rs 7.1B); management expects H2 seasonal demand to clear the inventory glut rather than discounting — consistent with the existing WATCH/re-evaluate-at-Q3 stance, no change warranted. MEBL — no new news beyond the already-processed Sep 2 sukuk congratulatory note; Rs 8/share dividend payment lands Sep 10 (ex-date Aug 18 already passed, fully reflected). FABL — checked again, still no published ex-date for the Aug 6 Rs 1.50/share interim (a May 6, 2026 ex-date appearing in some data feeds is from an earlier, unrelated dividend cycle — not this one). AVN — no new company announcements since the Aug 28 H1 filing; the 'next earnings Sep 2' flagged by one data aggregator appears to be a stale/incorrect placeholder, not an actual new release — EXIT call unexecuted through 7 reviews now. DATA QUALITY: stock prices refreshed normally. Fund NAVs (funds_updated: Aug 13) are now 21 days stale — the MUFAP scraper issue remains unresolved; ~30% of portfolio value (all 7 funds) is still being priced off a 3-week-old NAV snapshot, a growing blind spot needing a real fix.

actions.title: Avanceon — H1 report confirms swing to a real net loss; EXIT call now backed by hard numbers, still unexecuted
actions.detail: No new news since the Aug 28 H1/Q2 FY26 filing: consolidated H1 2026 revenue grew a healthy +34% YoY (Rs 7.04B) but the company swung from a Rs 168M profit to a Rs 260M NET LOSS (EPS −Rs 0.62 vs +Rs 0.38); Q2 alone the loss widened to Rs 317M (EPS −Rs 0.74) from a Rs 104M loss a year earlier. Standalone tells the same story (H1 swung from +Rs 136M profit to −Rs 66M loss). No dividend declared (NIL). Cause: admin/selling expenses up 45% YoY, far outpacing revenue growth, plus 'other income' that cushioned last year's profit (Rs 162M in H1 2025) collapsed to Rs 77M this year, exposing weak core operating economics. This is real, board-confirmed deterioration — not a rumor or a single bad line item. Now Rs 29.18, −35.3% on cost, still near the post-selloff lows after giving back the Aug 31 bounce. No further earnings catalyst is pending before Q3; there is no reason left to keep waiting. The Aug 25 EXIT call is unexecuted through 7 reviews now — recommend selling the entire position at market.
